readmeExcerpt: # Skills For Designers and Engineers For designers and engineers to help them build better user interfaces. Knowing whether you made a right choice when it comes to animations, or design in general, is hard. These skills aim to help you get to those right decisions faster. They are based on my years of experience working at companies like Vercel and Linear. All the skills here are a side-effect of domain-expertise. AI doesn’t replace such expertise, it amplifies what you can get out of it and makes you way better relative to others. So learn to code, design, or develop expertise in any other field. It’s extremely valuable. You can stay up to date with my skills here: [Sign Up To The Newsletter](https://aiforui.dev/newsletter) ## Install ```bash npx skills@latest add emilkowalski/skills ``` Every skill page at [aiforui.dev/skills](https://aiforui.dev/skills) shows when to use the skill, an example of the result, and prompts to try. ## Why use it? Agents don’t have great taste I have seen plenty of times that agents don’t pick the right ingredients for an animation. An `ease-in` easing for an enter animation when it’s supposed to be `ease-out` ([here’s why](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/7-practical-animation-tips#4.-choose-the-right-easing)). Or they choose a solid border instead of a semi-transparent shadow for your UIs. All these small things compound and make your interface either amazing, or just... not that great. As explained in [Agents with Taste](https://emilkowal.ski/ui/agents-with-taste), these skills list all the little mistakes agents can potentially make and explain how to fix them. This is your shortcut to great interfaces. A shortcut to stand out in a sea of slop. ## Reference - **[emil-design-eng](https://aiforui.dev/skills/emil-design-eng)** — The main skill that consists of mostly animation, but also some design advice. - **[animate](https://aiforui.dev/skills/animate)** — Builds an animation from scratch while choosing the correct curve, duration, properties, and so on. - **[animate-expo](https://aiforui.dev/skills/animate-expo)** — The same bar, for React Native and Expo: gestures, sheets, haptics, screen transitions, and keeping motion off the JS thread. - **[review-animations](https://aiforui.dev/skills/review-animations)** — Review your animations in a strict way, based on my rules. - **[improve-animations](https://aiforui.dev/skills/improve-animations)** — Audit all the animations in your codebase and get prioritized, self-contained plans that any agent can execute. - **[find-animation-opportunities](https://aiforui.dev/skills/find-animation-opportunities)** — Search your UI for places that would genuinely benefit from motion, while also telling you what not to animate. - **[remove-animations](https://aiforui.dev/skills/remove-animations)** — The opposite of finding opportunities: remove the animations your app doesn't need, think of motion on keyboard shortcuts, fade-ins on every section, and delay on every tooltip in a group. - **[choreograph](https://aiforui.dev/skills/choreograph)** — Coordinate several elements that animate together: what leads, what follows, what runs in parallel, and what shouldn't move at all. - **[animation-performance](https://aiforui.dev/skills/animation-performance)** — Fix animations that drop frames. It includes lots of subtle issues that most agents miss. - **[animation-vocabulary](https://aiforui.dev/skills/animation-vocabulary)** — Get better animations from an AI by telling it exactly what you want by using the right words. - **[apple-design](https://aiforui.dev/skills/apple-design)** — Apple’s principles for interface design and fluid motion, distilled from their WWDC design talks and translated for the web. - **[gestures](https://aiforui.dev/skills/gestures)** — Build drag, swipe, and sheet interactions that track the finger 1:1, carry the speed of the release, and can be caught mid-animation. - **[pick-ui-library](https://aiforui.dev/skills/pick-ui-library)** — Have your agent pick the right library for the task based on libraries I use and trust, instead of letting AI hand-roll a toast component or install an abandoned package. - **[prototype](https://aiforui.dev/skills/prototype)** — Build multiple different versions of a UI piece you describe and go through them using a switcher. - **[mobile-native](https://aiforui.dev/skills/mobile-native)** — Make your web app feel native on a phone: sticky hover states, tap highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, safe areas, and the rest of the small fixes that separate a website from an app. - **[break-ui](https://aiforui.dev/skills/break-ui)** — Try to break the UI you built with worst-case data: long names, unusual emails, one-letter names, huge counts, empty lists, long labels. - **[learn-taste](https://aiforui.dev/skills/learn-taste)** — Run it at the end of a session. It collects every design correction you made, including the edits you made yourself, and turns each one into a rule with its reason in your `DESIGN.md`, so the next agent doesn’t make the same mistake. - **[ask-emil](https://aiforui.dev/skills/ask-emil)** — Not sure which skill to use? Describe your situation and it points you to the right skill, or the right sequence of them, from idea to shipped. - **[ask-sonner](https://aiforui.dev/skills/ask-sonner)** — Your guide to working with [Sonner](https://sonner.emilkowal.ski), my toast library. Contains setup, styling, recipes, and fixes for the most common issues.
readmeHtml:
Skills For Designers and Engineers

For designers and engineers to help them build better user interfaces.

Knowing whether you made a right choice when it comes to animations, or design in general, is hard. These skills aim to help you get to those right decisions faster.

They are based on my years of experience working at companies like Vercel and Linear.

All the skills here are a side-effect of domain-expertise. AI doesn’t replace such expertise, it amplifies what you can get out of it and makes you way better relative to others.

So learn to code, design, or develop expertise in any other field. It’s extremely valuable.

You can stay up to date with my skills here:

Sign Up To The Newsletter

Install

npx skills@latest add emilkowalski/skills

Every skill page at aiforui.dev/skills shows when to use the skill, an example of the result, and prompts to try.

Why use it?

Agents don’t have great taste

I have seen plenty of times that agents don’t pick the right ingredients for an animation. An ease-in easing for an enter animation when it’s supposed to be ease-out (here’s why). Or they choose a solid border instead of a semi-transparent shadow for your UIs.

All these small things compound and make your interface either amazing, or just... not that great.

As explained in Agents with Taste, these skills list all the little mistakes agents can potentially make and explain how to fix them.

This is your shortcut to great interfaces. A shortcut to stand out in a sea of slop.

Reference

  • emil-design-eng — The main skill that consists of mostly animation, but also some design advice.
  • animate — Builds an animation from scratch while choosing the correct curve, duration, properties, and so on.
  • animate-expo — The same bar, for React Native and Expo: gestures, sheets, haptics, screen transitions, and keeping motion off the JS thread.
  • review-animations — Review your animations in a strict way, based on my rules.
  • improve-animations — Audit all the animations in your codebase and get prioritized, self-contained plans that any agent can execute.
  • find-animation-opportunities — Search your UI for places that would genuinely benefit from motion, while also telling you what not to animate.
  • remove-animations — The opposite of finding opportunities: remove the animations your app doesn't need, think of motion on keyboard shortcuts, fade-ins on every section, and delay on every tooltip in a group.
  • choreograph — Coordinate several elements that animate together: what leads, what follows, what runs in parallel, and what shouldn't move at all.
  • animation-performance — Fix animations that drop frames. It includes lots of subtle issues that most agents miss.
  • animation-vocabulary — Get better animations from an AI by telling it exactly what you want by using the right words.
  • apple-design — Apple’s principles for interface design and fluid motion, distilled from their WWDC design talks and translated for the web.
  • gestures — Build drag, swipe, and sheet interactions that track the finger 1:1, carry the speed of the release, and can be caught mid-animation.
  • pick-ui-library — Have your agent pick the right library for the task based on libraries I use and trust, instead of letting AI hand-roll a toast component or install an abandoned package.
  • prototype — Build multiple different versions of a UI piece you describe and go through them using a switcher.
  • mobile-native — Make your web app feel native on a phone: sticky hover states, tap highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom the page, laggy taps, safe areas, and the rest of the small fixes that separate a website from an app.
  • break-ui — Try to break the UI you built with worst-case data: long names, unusual emails, one-letter names, huge counts, empty lists, long labels.
  • learn-taste — Run it at the end of a session. It collects every design correction you made, including the edits you made yourself, and turns each one into a rule with its reason in your DESIGN.md, so the next agent doesn’t make the same mistake.
  • ask-emil — Not sure which skill to use? Describe your situation and it points you to the right skill, or the right sequence of them, from idea to shipped.
  • ask-sonner — Your guide to working with Sonner, my toast library. Contains setup, styling, recipes, and fixes for the most common issues.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A curated repository of advanced design and animation principles tailored for frontend design engineers.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: This repository acts as a highly specialized knowledge base bridging the gap between visual design and frontend engineering. It codifies complex design decisions, particularly concerning UI animation, micro-interactions, and spatial layouts, into actionable technical advice. Rather than providing generic CSS snippets, it breaks down the underlying physics, timing functions, and psychological impacts of specific UI behaviors. The content is structured to help engineers evaluate whether a specific animation enhances usability or introduces friction. It serves as a masterclass in building interfaces that feel exceptionally polished and responsive.
keyFeatures: Animation Physics: Details the mathematical principles behind spring animations and easing curves for natural-feeling motion.
Interaction Audits: Provides frameworks for evaluating the necessity and impact of complex micro-interactions.
Spatial Reasoning: Explains advanced layout techniques and the psychological implications of whitespace and typography scaling.
Performance Considerations: Links aesthetic decisions directly to browser rendering performance and hardware acceleration.
Actionable Heuristics: Codifies subjective design taste into objective rules that engineers can apply during implementation.

useCases.title: UI Polish
useCases.description: Frontend engineers consult the animation physics guidelines to replace linear CSS transitions with fluid, interruptible spring physics.

useCases.title: Design System Construction
useCases.description: Designers use the documented heuristics to establish firm rules for motion and spatial scaling within corporate design systems.

useCases.title: Performance Debugging
useCases.description: Developers optimize slow interactions by applying the repository's guidelines on triggering hardware acceleration during complex layout shifts.

useCases.title: Cross-Discipline Communication
useCases.description: Engineers use the specific terminology provided to effectively communicate technical constraints to UI designers.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers, UX/UI designers, and design engineers focused on creating high-quality, deeply interactive web interfaces. Requires an understanding of CSS, DOM rendering, and basic design principles.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: Read through the core documentation files in the repository to understand the foundational heuristics.
